 6-year-old boy killed, mother seriously injured in house fire on Detroit’s west side
 Two older siblings were able to escape prior to the fire department’s arrival, officials said
 Jenny Sherman , Digital Content Producer
 Published:  November 19, 2026 at 5:51 AM Updated:  November 19, 2026 at 6:23 AM Tags:  Detroit DETROIT – An investigation is underway into the cause of a fire that killed a 6-year-old boy and critically injured his mother at a home on Detroit’s west side overnight.
 Firefighters responded to the home on Lawrence Street between Linwood and Dexter within five minutes of receiving a call about the fire around 2:12 a.m. Upon arrival, the first and second floors of the home were fully engulfed and crews were notified by neighbors that there were people trapped inside.
 Detroit Fire Department Battalion Chief Jeffrey Urbas says firefighters located the child dead on the first floor during an aggressive interior search of the home. Fire crews were able to locate and rescue the child’s mother near the back of the home. 
 Urbas said the mother had no pulse when she was found but EMS was able to revive her at the scene. She was transported to a nearby hospital where she is listed in critical condition.
 Two older siblings were able to get out of the home prior to the fire department’s arrival who are also being treated at an area hospital.
 The fire also extended to a home next door that was occupied but empty at the time, which fire crews said they were able to save.
 The cause of the fire remains under investigation and DFD officials say the city will “wrap its arms around the family and provide any resources we can as they work to heal and recover.”
